description: We are a second- and third-year team software Engineering students that look for to take on new challenges and put our skills and knowledge to the test. We are motivated by the opportunity to tackle real-world problems, and apply what we have learned throughout our academic journey, and explore new ways of approaching them.
summary: We developed a comprehensive health-care assistance software for astronauts. Daily monitoring is essential because the body doesn't behave the same way in hostile environments like space, the Moon, or Mars. We also consider this a vital issue to address because we provide the necessary tools for them to manage on their own when needed. Since communication with Earth has a delay of at least 20 minutes—and in critical situations time is everything—we created this assistant to guide them clearly and concisely through voice or text, providing immediate, verified information for any scenarios that may arise.
details:
M.A.L.I. is a 100% offline comprehensive biometric monitoring and clinical support platform designed to guide crew members through voice commands regarding their own health or a teammate's condition in various hostile environments.

It simplifies handling medical emergencies without requiring advanced medical knowledge. It actively feeds back information without exposing crew members to invasive procedures.

Our project aims to provide a complete solution for various situations they might face by guiding astronauts in a clear, step-by-step manner. Additionally, it allows for task delegation based on each individual's situation.

Super-intelligences were used to develop the foundations, followed by HTML coding.

M.A.L.I. is innovative in data collection through various automated biomarkers, allowing crew members to stick to their routine and focus on their respective tasks. It also features three modes with different functional focuses: Rover mode (lunar/martian exploration), Route mode (spacecraft in transit), and Space Station mode (International Space Station).

Factors such as ease of use, avoiding information overload, supporting crew members during stressful situations together, and data collection innovation were all taken into account.
